abstract:
Online scams are increasing rapidly and have become a pervasive feature of digital marketplaces, causing substantial harm to consumers. We conceptualize online scams as
                    AI-driven malicious persuasion attempts
                    and illustrate how AI makes their creation and execution easier (i.e.,
                    simplicity
                    ) while increasing their
                    sophistication
                    and
                    scale
                    . Taking an integrated persuasion knowledge and dynamic consumer vulnerability perspective, we further explain how consumer vulnerability can both increase susceptibility to malicious persuasion attempts and emerge or intensify as a consequence of victimization. To counter the resulting challenges, we argue that consumer empowerment is needed to complement regulation and self-regulation. Specifically, we focus on consumers’ ability to
                    recognize
                    and
                    resist
                    AI-driven malicious persuasion attempts,
                    report
                    victimization, and develop
                    resilience
                    through recovery and adaptation over time. We identify corresponding interventions and derive avenues for future research and public policy implications.

ur.ai_reason: AI驱动诈骗为核心议题，消费者脆弱性/说服知识是CX核心
ur.tldr: 将在线诈骗概念化为AI驱动的恶意说服行为，揭示AI如何使诈骗更易生成、更复杂且更具规模。基于说服知识与动态消费者脆弱性框架，解释脆弱性如何同时增加受骗风险并因受害而加剧。主张通过消费者赋权（识别、抵抗、举报、恢复韧性）来补充监管与自律，并提出干预措施与未来研究方向。

title: EXPRESS: The AI-Driven Scam Economy: Persuasion Knowledge, Consumer Vulnerability, and Empowerment
title_zh: EXPRESS：AI驱动的诈骗经济：说服知识、消费者脆弱性与赋权
